ADR-011 RESTORATION (2026-08-16): the 'no content checks on IBR items anywhere in this case' rule quoted above was wrong, and it is the reason this note exists. It rested on specs/001-sec10k-contract.md's line 'For any other status: start/end are null' -- a line the extractor never implemented, since classify() can only return incorporated_by_reference when a heading was found, so IBR items have always carried real offsets. The rule therefore deleted anchors from correctly-located spans on the authority of a spec line the code did not honour. ADR-011 settles it the other way: IBR items carry pointer-text offsets, and INV-S1, verbatim and layer-8 boundary hygiene now cover those spans (the content-shape validators still do not -- their thresholds were measured over extracted spans and a pointer paragraph has no vocabulary to judge). Restored here: items 6, 7, 7A and 8, whose spans are the pointer paragraphs naming the 2001 Annual Report to Shareholders and its page ranges -- the exact text a human inspector reads to confirm an IBR claim. All four anchors verified 2026-08-16 by grep -c -F against the raw fixture, each returning exactly 1: 'The information appearing under "Selected Financial Information" on page 61' (item 6), '"Management's Discussion and Analysis," appearing on pages 19 through 32' (item 7), '"Quantitative Risks Measures," appearing on page 30 of our 2001 Annual' (item 7A), 'Ernst & Young LLP dated January 24, 2002, and supplementary information' (item 8). Each sits on a single physical line of the fixed-width text, same anti-wrap convention as the rest of this case.
